body: This movie delves into the deep scars of childhood and how they shape us for life, and the search for identitity, balancing pain with just the right amount of humour. Beautifully written and wonderful acting, that had us crying and laughing all at the same time. Finally a movie that really makes you "feel" something inside.

Den Sidste Viking Is the story about family, and how a man want he weird brother, to tell him where he hidden the loot.

Anders Thomas Jensen Knows, what story he wants to tell, and he is very good at it at this point.

Story about people who are outsiders of society, and people with diagnoses who doesn't fit in to normal Society. And does it with black comedy and heartfelt moments.

The movie was for me very funny, but it just hit the perfect tone shifting ability, so it never felt jarring.

The actors to a great job, and especially Mads Mikkelsen who plays, a neurodivergent person very well and with humanity.

The story is great and a lot of fun. There's only one twist that put a little bad taste in my mouth, but the movie is still good.

I left the movie theater with a lot of facts, about IKEA and the Holocaust. It a great time would recommend.

Danish dark comedy can be quite grotesque. If you're not familiar with, or a fan of Anders Thomas Jensen's other work, there's a good chance that you're going to find this movie unpleasantly bizarre.

If you are a fan of Anders Thomas Jensen, however, I am pleased to tell you that this is one of his best movies yet.

I am seriously not sure if Anders Thomas Jensen (writer and instructor) has been substituted with an AI language model recently! To me this movie is a boil-up of many of the previous movies written and instructed by ATJ (many of which I love!). This movie is far too violent for me and the plot even more wacky than "Mænd og høns" or "Adams æbler". Come to think of it, what has really carried the weight of many of the best movies by ATJ is Ole Thestrup, who has sadly passed away some years ago. I had high expectations (which is always dangerous) prior to watching this movie, but I really don't find it particularly good.

The Last Viking is an unexpected gem-equal parts hilarious, heartfelt, and thrilling. Mads Mikkelsen delivers yet another standout performance, bringing intense charisma and surprising comedic timing to a role that feels tailor-made for him.

The film strikes a perfect balance between humor and drama. The comedy never undercuts the emotional weight of the story; instead, it enhances it, giving the characters real charm and making the world feel alive. The acting across the board is fantastic, but Mikkelsen's presence anchors the whole movie.

What truly elevates The Last Viking is its clever, well-constructed plot. It's clear that a lot of thought went into the story-from its smart pacing to the meaningful character arcs and the engaging twists that keep you invested the whole way through. It's both entertaining and surprisingly thoughtful, offering more depth than you might expect from a Viking adventure-comedy.

Overall, The Last Viking is a delightful and memorable experience. It's funny, brilliantly acted, and crafted with care. Highly recommended.
